faq: It is a mean-motion estimate: right to within roughly half a day in most cycles, occasionally more. Almanac-grade ages come from full lunar ephemerides; this page's model is the standard synodic approximation every phase site shares.

27.3 days is the sidereal month — one orbit against the stars. Phases follow the synodic month (29.53) because the Earth has moved along its own orbit meanwhile, and the Sun-Moon geometry needs two extra days to repeat.
Can age be fractional and negative?
Fractional, yes — the age is a continuous count, so 11.1 days is normal output. It never goes negative; the count resets at each new moon, by definition of 'since the most recent'.
Does the age depend on my location?

The Moon's phase is essentially a whole-Earth fact at a given instant — location changes the view's tilt, not the age. Dates are read in UTC-anchored terms; a date near a boundary can straddle two ages across timezones.
A blue moon is a calendar accident — the second full moon inside one calendar month — not an age at all. Its age is the usual ~14.8 days; the calendar, not the Moon, did something odd.
How do I find a birthday Moon?
Enter the birth date: the age returned is the phase you were born under. Astrologers make much of it; astronomers merely confirm the number.

Two views of one geometry: age counts days along the cycle, illumination the lit fraction of the disc, computed by the Moon Illumination Calculator. Age 7.4 and 22.1 days both give 50% lit — waxing and waning halves.
